title: Escalation Policy Version Mismatch During On-Call Handoff
scenario_text:
**PagerDuty — Escalation Policy: 'Platform Services' (current version, effective May 5, 2026)**
Level 1: Primary on-call (5 min timeout)
Level 2: Secondary on-call (10 min timeout)
Level 3: SRE Manager (@nadia.okonkwo) (15 min timeout)
Level 4: VP Engineering (@divya.patel)
Schedule: Weekly rotation, handoff Mondays 09:00 UTC

**PagerDuty — Escalation Policy: 'Platform Services' (previous version, effective Jan 15 - May 4, 2026)**
Level 1: Primary on-call (5 min timeout)
Level 2: Engineering Manager of owning team (10 min timeout)
Level 3: SRE IC on-call (@jordan.kim or @alex.martinez) (10 min timeout)
Level 4: VP Engineering (@divya.patel)

**Slack — #sre-team (May 2, 2026, 2:33 PM)**
@nadia.okonkwo: Heads up — I'm updating the Platform Services escalation policy on Monday. Removing the EM from L2 since they never acknowledged anyway. Going straight to secondary on-call, then me, then Divya.
@jordan.kim: Makes sense. Are you updating the runbook too?
@nadia.okonkwo: Will do after the PD change goes live.
:+1: (3 reactions: @jordan.kim, @alex.martinez, @priya.singh)

**Confluence — 'Platform Services Runbook' (last edited: Jan 18, 2026)**
Section 5 — Escalation Path:
'If primary on-call does not acknowledge within 5 minutes, PagerDuty escalates to the Engineering Manager of the owning squad. If EM does not ack within 10 minutes, the SRE Incident Commander on rotation is paged. Final escalation: VP Engineering.'
Note: This section has not been updated since January.

**PagerDuty — Incident #INC-4512 (May 9, 2026, 02:14 UTC)**
Triggered: 'Database connection pool exhaustion on platform-auth'
Severity: HIGH
Timeline:
- 02:14: Primary on-call @priya.singh paged. No ack.
- 02:19: Escalated to Level 2. @alex.martinez (secondary) paged. No ack.
- 02:29: Escalated to Level 3. @nadia.okonkwo paged. Acknowledged at 02:31.
- 02:31: Nadia opened war room. Issue resolved by 02:58.

**Jira — PLAT-8821 'INC-4512 Postmortem' (Created May 9, 2026)**
Comment (@priya.singh, May 9, 10:00 AM): 'My phone was on DND — that's on me. But I want to flag: the runbook says EM gets paged at L2. I assumed if I missed it, my EM @chen.wei would be the next page. I didn't realize the policy changed last Monday.'
Comment (@chen.wei, May 9, 10:45 AM): 'I was never notified the escalation path changed. First I'm hearing of it.'
Comment (@nadia.okonkwo, May 9, 11:00 AM): 'I posted in #sre-team about this. The Confluence update is on my backlog.'

**Slack — DM @priya.singh to @jordan.kim (May 9, 2026, 10:15 AM)**
@priya.singh: Hey — honest question. If I'd followed the runbook (which says EM at L2), would that have been wrong? Like am I responsible for checking PD directly vs trusting the runbook?
@jordan.kim: Technically PD is the system of record for escalation routing. But yeah, I get the confusion. We'll address it in the postmortem.
question: In the INC-4512 postmortem, was the escalation path that PagerDuty followed on May 9 correct according to the current authoritative escalation policy?

contributor.name: Jordan Kim
contributor.title: Senior Site Reliability Engineer / Incident Commander
contributor.domain_expertise: Incident response, change management, SLA enforcement, postmortem process

choices: Partially — the escalation path was correct but the timing was wrong; Level 2 should have had a 10-minute timeout but only waited 5 minutes before escalating to Level 3
Yes — PagerDuty is the system of record for escalation routing, the policy was updated May 5, and the system correctly escalated Primary -> Secondary -> SRE Manager
No — the Confluence runbook is the authoritative escalation reference and it specifies EM at Level 2, which PagerDuty skipped
No — Nadia's policy change was never formally approved; the Slack thumbsup reactions do not constitute a valid change approval per Meridian's change management policy
